{{Quote|No games on my ship!|Yaru Korsin, to Devore Korsin|<ref name="precipice" />}}
A '''duel''' occurred in [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], in the wreckage of the ''[[Omen]]'', a [[Sith dreadnaught]] that crash-landed on the uncharted [[Planet/Legends|planet]] of [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]] during the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]]. The [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|battle]] was waged between the half-brothers [[Yaru Korsin|Yaru]] and [[Devore Korsin]], over who would [[Commander/Legends|command]] the rest of the ''Omen''{{'s}} surviving crew. After a tense argument in the remains of their [[Starship/Legends|ship]], Devore, who desired his brother's post as [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of the ''Omen'', attacked Yaru while under the influence of [[Red Rage]] [[Spice/Legends|spice]]. The [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]] continued outside the teetering dreadnaught, and, although Devore briefly gained the upper hand, Yaru regained the advantage after using the ship itself as a weapon. After being hit squarely in the shoulder by one of the ''Omen''{{'s}} [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedo]] tube doors, Devore ended up covered in rubble just [[Meter/Legends|meters]] from the edge of a steep [[Takara Mountains|cliff]]&mdash;although Devore was incapacitated, Yaru decided to drop his brother off the ledge to his [[Death/Legends|death]].

==Prelude==
{{Quote|Back at Primus Goluud. On the station. You met with Sadow, didn't you?''"<br />"''To discuss the Lignan operation.''"<br />"''You weren't discussing something else? Like who should command this mission? You were discussing who would command this mission. What did you say when he said no?|Yaru Korsin and Devore Korsin, in a discussion that would lead to their duel|<ref name="precipice" />}}
In [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], at the height of the [[Great Hyperspace War/Legends|Great Hyperspace War]], [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] sent the<ref name="precipice" /> [[Sith dreadnaught]]<ref name="crosscurrent">''[[Crosscurrent]]''</ref> ''[[Omen]]'' on a [[Lignan crystal|Lignan]] [[Mining/Legends|mining]] and delivery mission to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Phaegon III]]'s [[Phaegon III's largest moon|largest moon]]. Among the ''Omen''{{'s}} crew were [[Yaru Korsin|Yaru]] and [[Devore Korsin]], half-brothers with a contentious relationship&mdash;Yaru was mission leader, while Devore headed the mining team. As the ''Omen'' prepared to [[Transport/Legends|transport]] their Lignan [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] from Phaegon III to their destination on the planet [[Kirrek]], a [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Skirmish over Phaegon III|attack]] resulted in the [[Starship/Legends|ship]] being knocked off course as it jumped to [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]].<ref name="precipice" />

The severely-damaged ''Omen'' crash-landed on an uncharted planet known as [[Kesh/Legends|Kesh]]. Although the Korsin brothers both survived the crash along with many of the crew, tensions soon arose over which Korsin would [[Commander/Legends|command]] the rest of the castaways, and the remaining [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] on Kesh were in dire straits. Desperate to find a way off Kesh, Devore unsuccessfully searched the ''Omen''{{'s}} wreckage<ref name="precipice" /> in the [[Takara Mountains|Cetajan Mountains]].<ref name="skyborn">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]''</ref> Defeated, Devore collapsed in the [[Captain/Legends|captain's]] chair and took a dose of [[Red Rage]] [[Spice/Legends|spice]]. Yaru soon entered the ship as well, similarly trying to discover a means to facilitate their escape. An argument ensued between the two brothers, regarding whether there was any hope for their survival&mdash;eventually, Yaru broached the subject of a meeting that Devore had with Naga Sadow shortly before the mission started, where Devore unsuccessfully petitioned for command. Things grew more tense between the Korsins, and Devore, under the influence of spice, reacted in an outburst of rage and attacked.<ref name="precipice" />

==The duel==
{{Quote|It's over, Yaru. We should have done this before. It's been decided. ''I'm'' Commander Korsin.|Devore Korsin, to Yaru Korsin|<ref name="precipice" />}}
His natural rage and strength enhanced by the Red Rage spice, Devore used his [[Force-sensitive/Legends|connection]] to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to create a [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force Whirlwind|whirlwind]], which turned nearby debris, including jagged pieces of [[Transparisteel/Legends|transparisteel]], into weapons that caused superficial wounds to Yaru's face. Yaru was able to [[Force barrier/Legends|shield]] himself before he took too much damage, and he flung his brother out of the teetering ''Omen''. However, as Yaru stepped out of the ruined starship, he was distracted by a [[Uvak|large winged creature]] that seemed to be observing the battle. That diverted Yaru's attention long enough for Devore to gain the upper hand, throwing Yaru against the ''Omen''{{'s}} wreckage.<ref name="precipice" />

Emboldened by his advantage, Devore proclaimed himself to be the true "Commander Korsin." From there, the fighting turned into an all-out [[Lightsaber duel/Legends|lightsaber duel]], although Devore found his furious [[Lightsaber combat/Legends|attacks]] repeatedly parried. Thinking on his feet, Yaru attempted to fire a [[Torpedo/Legends|torpedo]] from the ''Omen''{{'s}} exterior tubes by manipulating the control box from the outside&mdash;however, the doors were partially stuck in the ground, and, although the torpedo did not emerge, the doors hit Devore in the shoulder and sent him flying. Devore came to a stop at the edge of a sheer cliff overlooking a nearby [[Ocean/Legends|ocean]], and, partially covered with rubble, he was gravely wounded and unable to see. Although Yaru considered helping his brother, he decided against it, allowing Devore to drop off the ledge to his [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="precipice" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|I saw you.''"<br />"''What?''"<br />"''I saw you a second time on the mountain, that day. You threw something over the side. I saw you throw something, I didn't know what&ndash;until you sent me to return to the village. I flew down there, Korsin. I saw him below, on the rocks. He was a man, like you.|Adari Vaal and Yaru Korsin, discussing what she observed of the duel|<ref name="skyborn" />}}
By chance, the battle was witnessed by native [[Keshiri/Legends|Keshiri]] [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Adari Vaal]], who was riding the winged uvak that had distracted Yaru during the duel. With her help, the surviving Sith convinced the rest of the Keshiri that they were their [[Deity/Legends|gods]], the [[Skyborn]], with Yaru proclaimed as [[Grand Lord]] of Kesh.<ref name="skyborn" /> The crew of the ''Omen'' and their descendants formed a [[Lost Tribe of Sith|Sith tribe]] that survived for thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]].<ref name="omen">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Omen]]''</ref> Devore Korsin was not forgotten by his [[Korsin family|family]]&mdash;although his wife, [[Seelah Korsin|Seelah]], [[Marriage/Legends|married]] Yaru and [[Reproduction/Legends|had]] a daughter, [[Nida Korsin|Nida]], with him, she secretly plotted to avenge her husband's death. Her plot was carried out in [[4975 BBY]], when Seelah arranged for her and Devore's son, [[Jariad Korsin|Jariad]], to [[Duel near the Kesh Sith Temple|attack]] Grand [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Korsin with a group of [[Sith Saber|Sith warriors]]. Although Yaru died during the skirmish, Jariad was also killed and Seelah incapacitated. Nida, who fought along with her [[Parent/Legends|father]], became the new Grand Lord.<ref name="savior">''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The duel first appeared in ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Precipice]]'', a [[2009]] [[eBook]] written by [[John Jackson Miller]].<ref name="precipice" /> It was also briefly featured during the eBook's follow-up, ''[[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Skyborn]]'',<ref name="skyborn" /> along with mentions in [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Paragon|two]]<ref name="paragon" /> [[Lost Tribe of the Sith: Savior|other]] sequels.<ref name="savior" /> An image of Adari Vaal observing the duel was included in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.<ref name="Companion">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref>
